Any person who would like to address the Legislative Bodies on any agendized item is requested to complete a speaker card for the City Clerk/Agency/Authority Secretary and identify the agenda item you would like to discuss. Each person will be given an opportunity to address the Legislative Body at the time such item is discussed. Speaker cards are available at the rear of the Council Chambers and your speaker card must be filled out prior to the agenda item being called. We respectfully request that you fill the cards out completely and print as clearly as possible. Following this procedure will allow for a smooth and timely process for the meeting and we appreciate your cooperation. Individual speakers are limited to three (3) minutes each.
Consent Calendar items under the Legislative Body may be acted upon with one motion, a second and the vote. If you desire to speak on an item or items on the Consent Calendar, you may fill out one speaker card for the Consent Calendar. You will be given three minutes to address your concerns before the Legislative Body takes action on the Consent Calendar.

At each regular City Council Meeting, the City Council is presented with check and ACH/wire registers listing the financial claims (invoices) against the City for purchase of materials, supplies, services, and capital projects issued the prior three to four weeks. This process provides the City Council the opportunity to review the expenditures of the City. Claims are paid via checks, Automated Clearing House (ACH) payments, or federal wires. The justifying backup information for each expenditure is available in the Finance Department.

CC 10. Accept Public Works Construction Project No. 17-009, 5th Street East Corridor Improvements ATPL-5419(046), constructed by C.A. Rasmussen, Inc., and direct the City Clerk to file the Notice of Completion for the project. Retention on this project will be disbursed in accordance with California Public Contract Code.
The 5th Street East Corridor, from Avenue H-8 to Avenue J-4, was constructed based on the need for safety improvements for students walking or bicycling to and from school. This corridor is adjacent to three public schools: El Dorado Elementary, Linda Verde Elementary, and Piute Middle School. The improvements included the construction of pedestrian curb bulb-outs, with ADA compliant curb ramps to shorten crossing distance at several locations along 5th Street East, and new traffic striping installed buffered bike lanes. These improvements are in compliance with the Master Plan of Trails and Bikeways.

CC 11. Approve Task Order No. 1 with Encompass Consultant Group, Inc., of Lancaster, CA, in accordance with the Multi-Year Professional Services Agreement in the amount of $438,105.80 with a 10% contingency; and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to sign all documents.
This project will improve safety and shorten the crossing distance for pedestrians by constructing sidewalks and pathways with high visibility crosswalks, curb extensions/bulb-outs. The proposed bike lanes with painted buffers will provide bicyclists space separation from the high speed vehicular traffic. This project will encourage walking and bicycling among all users by increasing safety and mobility with connections to transit access points and local destinations. The proposed project is about 2.68 miles in length on two major arterial streets. The project limits are: Avenue J from 10th Street West to Challenger Way, and 10th Street West from Lancaster Boulevard to Avenue J.

This contract is awarded to the lowest responsible bidder per California Public Code Section 22038 (b).
In 2015, the City of Lancaster set an ambitious goal of renewing, repairing or replacing every lane mile of public roadway within the City by 2025. To date, the City has completed more than 40 road projects, which have revived approximately 396 lane-miles of roads. As part of the REVIVE 25 program, this project will repair and resurface approximately 41.25 lane-miles of City streets. The project areas include (1) neighborhood bounded by 10th Street West and 20th Street West; Avenue I to Lancaster Boulevard; (2) neighborhood bounded by Avenue J-8 and Avenue K; 10th Street West to Adler Avenue; (AA1) 30th Street West from Avenue M to Avenue N; (AA2) 4th Street East from Avenue L to Avenue M.

California Choice Energy Authority (CCEA) Board Recommendation:
Adopt the proposed CCEA Fiscal Year 2019-2020 Budget as presented.
The City is required to adopt a budget by July 1 of each year that establishes appropriations and estimated revenues for the upcoming fiscal year. The proposed budget is a culmination of many months of work by the City Council and staff in reviewing priorities and evaluating programs to meet those priorities, with a focus on maintaining responsive and relevant service for residents. City Council's priorities addressing: creation of a hybrid police model & addressing homelessness, creation of new revenue streams (fiber network system, streetlight cameras & Wi-Fi, and partnering with private companies), Medical Main Street, Parkway Village, Lancaster Choice Energy grant programs, citywide infrastructure renovations and modernization, major arterial/residential roadway improvements, freeway interchange improvements, IMPACT initiatives, and rebranding are addressed through the proposed FY 2019-2020 Budget.

PUBLIC HEARING
PH 1. Resolution Amending Lancaster Choice Energy Customer Power Generation Rate Schedule
Recommendation:
Adopt Resolution No. 19-39, amending Resolution No. 19-16 amending customer power generation rates for Lancaster Choice Energy effective June 1, 2019.
Lancaster Choice Energy ("LCE") has been serving customers since 2015. An essential part of LCE's operation is rate setting. A fundamental requirement in setting rates is to ensure sufficient revenue to cover LCE's operating expenses and provide for reserves. In addition to meeting these requirements, LCE's proposed rate schedule provides savings to LCE customers as compared to current SCE rates. The non-Time of Use Domestic rate is proposed to increase from $.07197/kWh to $.08031/kWh. Based on an average usage of 641 kWh (as determined by SCE), the proposed rate results in an average increase of $5.35 per month.

NB 2. Disposition and Development Agreement with Green Valley Land Management, LLC
Recommendation:
Authorize the City Manager or his designee to finalize and execute a Disposition and Development Agreement with Green Valley Land Management, LLC for the sale and subsequent development of APN 3125-009-908, an 11.4-acre commercial parcel; and authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute all related documents.
The vision for this effort was to position the City to capture new development opportunities for our community, including commercial and retail. Staff has received an offer for full appraised value for APN 3125-009-908, an 11.4-acre parcel located between 15th Street West and the 14 Freeway, just north of Avenue K-8. Green Valley Land Management, LLC is proposing the immediate development of a popular, family-friendly chain restaurant, which will occupy approximately 2.5 acres of the site. The remainder is planned for additional commercial development, with the potential for inclusion of a hotel in the future
NB 2
NB 2 attachment
Recommendation:
Adopt Resolution No. 19-40, supporting the designation of proposed U.S. Bicycle Route 85 (USBR85) through the City of Lancaster.
As part of a national effort, the American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials (AASHTO) is to build a U.S. Bicycle Route 85 system from northern to southern California; Caltrans, California Bicycle Coalition, and the Adventure Cycling Association have approached the City of Lancaster to support the proposed U.S. Bicycle Route 85 (USBR85), route through the City. The proposed route, starting near Fresno and ending at the California/Mexico border, would have approximately 12 miles that fall within the City of Lancaster. The route follows 50th Street West northbound at Avenue M, then turns west on Avenue L until 90th Street West where the route turns to go north past the City limits. Designating a USBR85 does not impose any constraints or restrictions on the use of a road, street, trail or right-of-way. Its current or future status or use for any other purpose is not changed. There is no requirement that roads for U.S. Bicycle Route 85 meet the guidelines in the AASHTO Guide for Bicycle Facilities.
